general.method_note: Unallocated reserves the council expects to hold at 31 March 2027 (RA 2026-27 line 1016).

minimum_safe.method_note: Revenue Budget and Council Tax Levels 2026/27, PDF page 35. Paragraph 83: general balances have a medium-term optimal range of £19m to £23m; this is the bottom of the range

levers.label: Council tax rise
levers.method_note: 1% of 2027/28 council tax before the rise: £98.2m ÷ (1 + 4.99%). The council's forecast already assumes a 4.99% rise, so only the difference from it closes or widens the gap.

levers.label: Further savings
levers.method_note: £1m chosen closes £1m of the gap, by definition. On top of the £8.0m of savings the forecast already includes.

levers.label: Use reserves
levers.method_note: £1m chosen closes £1m of the gap, by definition.

levers.label: Parking and fees
levers.method_note: 1% of the £80.5m of fees and charges income in the 2026/27 budget (Appendix I). Static: it assumes people use services as much at higher prices, and some fees are set by law (PRE_SHIP_REVIEW H5).

levers.label: Government settlement
levers.method_note: 1% of 2026/27 Revenue Support Grant plus retained business rates.

toggles.label: Add 20 law enforcement officers
toggles.method_note: Budget report, PDF page 23: 20 officers at the average cost of the Law Enforcement Team, which costs £4.6m a year for 72 officers
